After a few weeks, a workspace holds many agents, teams and workflows. Folders keep it readable.

## What you need

- Agentivity running, with the Studio open.

## Where folders are

Three lists have folders, each with its own:

- **Studio** > **Agents**, for agents and teams;
- **Studio** > **Workflows**, for workflows;
- **Resources** > **Data Tables**, for data tables.

In each list, the panel on the left shows the folders. A folder also appears as a line of the list, with **Folder** in the column **Type**.

## Create a folder

1. Open one of the three lists.
2. At the top of the panel on the left, select the folder button.
3. Type the **Folder name**, for example `Finance`.
4. Select **Create**.

## Put something in a folder

Drag a line of the list onto the folder, in the panel on the left.

To move several lines at once, hold Ctrl (or Cmd on a Mac), select the lines, then drag them.

## Look inside a folder

- Select the folder in the panel, or select **Open folder** on its line.
- The house button, at the top of the panel, goes back to the top level.

## Sub folders, rename, delete

Select the three dots on the line of a folder.

| Entry | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Add sub folder** | Creates a folder inside this one. |
| **Rename** | Changes the name of the folder. |
| **Move to root** | Takes the folder back to the top level. |
| **Delete** | Deletes the folder. |

Be careful with **Delete**: the Studio warns that "The folder and all its contents will be permanently deleted." Move what you want to keep out of the folder first.

## Good to know

- A folder changes only where something is filed. An agent in a folder works exactly as before, and a team can still use it as a member.
- In the list **Members** of a team, the agents are grouped by folder.
- A good first set of folders is one per department or per subject: `Finance`, `Support`, `Marketing`.
